name: CatalogPilot Connector
author: advisionecommerce

sections.description:
Turn Your WooCommerce Catalog Into a Competitive Advantage

CatalogPilot transforms ordinary WooCommerce product catalogs into intelligent, structured information designed for AI discovery, modern search and greater online visibility.

Retailers using CatalogPilot are already reporting improvements in product discovery and sales.

Experience it on your own products before spending anything.

30 days free. No credit card. No commitment.

We’ll enrich up to 50% of your qualifying catalog at no cost.

Like what you see? Subscribe and we’ll enrich the remaining qualifying catalog at no additional enrichment charge.

CatalogPilot then automatically maintains your catalog at 100% enrichment as products change or are added, with ongoing enrichment billed at transparent pay-as-you-go rates.

Your original WooCommerce catalog remains untouched.

CatalogPilot Connector links a WooCommerce store to the CatalogPilot service. It provides authenticated REST API endpoints that CatalogPilot uses to synchronize products, variations, categories, and approved catalog content.

When storefront delivery is enabled, the plugin can apply approved CatalogPilot titles, descriptions, metadata, structured data, and image attributes to supported WooCommerce pages. The storefront runtime is included in the plugin package and loaded through the WordPress script API.

A CatalogPilot account and a configured CatalogPilot site are required. WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Features include:

  • Authenticated, paginated catalog synchronization.
  • Product, variation, category, and image overlay storage in WordPress.
  • Storefront presentation of approved CatalogPilot content.
  • Multilingual product and category identity support.
  • Connection verification from the WordPress administration area.

External services

This plugin connects to the CatalogPilot software-as-a-service platform at catalog-pilot.com. The connection is necessary to synchronize catalog records, receive approved content, verify the configured site, and report storefront delivery activity.

CatalogPilot provisions the site identifier and HTTPS service URL after the WordPress administrator authorizes the connection. Plain HTTP service URLs are accepted only when WordPress reports a local or development environment and the URL uses a recognized local-development host. When the administrator verifies the connection, the plugin sends the site identifier, storefront URL, and connector version to the configured CatalogPilot service.

When CatalogPilot makes an authenticated catalog synchronization request, the plugin returns WooCommerce product, variation, and category records to CatalogPilot. Depending on the record type, these records include WordPress/WooCommerce object identifiers; names, descriptions, slugs, status, and storefront URLs; SKU, price, stock status, variation attributes, and category relationships; image identifiers and URLs; language and translation relationships; and creation, modification, or deletion timestamps. These records are sent only in response to a request authenticated with a WordPress application password and matching CatalogPilot site identifier. Customer, order, payment, and WordPress password data are not included.

When storefront delivery is enabled, the plugin may send the current page URL, language, page type, WooCommerce product/category/variation identifiers, image URLs and image text attributes, applied field names, and delivery context identifiers to CatalogPilot. This data is used to return the correct approved catalog content, resolve newly encountered catalog images, and measure whether approved content was delivered. Requests occur directly from the visitor’s browser while visitors view supported storefront pages, so CatalogPilot may also receive standard browser request information such as the visitor’s IP address, user agent, and referring URL, subject to the browser and storefront referrer policy. The plugin does not send WooCommerce customer passwords or payment details.

Approved rich descriptions may contain HTTPS images, video sources, or iframe embeds hosted by third parties. Iframe URLs are rendered only when their host and path match the allow rules configured for the CatalogPilot site. When this approved media appears on a storefront page, the visitor’s browser connects directly to the media provider. The provider may receive standard browser request information such as the visitor’s IP address, user agent, and referring URL, subject to the browser and storefront referrer policy. Which providers are contacted depends on the store’s approved catalog content; each provider’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

CatalogPilot terms: Terms and Conditions

CatalogPilot privacy policy: Privacy Policy

Support

For help connecting CatalogPilot, synchronizing a WooCommerce catalog, or delivering approved CatalogPilot content, email woo-support@catalog-pilot.com. Include the WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP, and CatalogPilot Connector versions when reporting a problem.

CatalogPilot support covers this connector and its CatalogPilot service integration. General WordPress, WooCommerce, hosting, theme, and unrelated third-party plugin support remains with those respective providers.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. If replacing another CatalogPilot distribution, deactivate and delete that package first. Do not install multiple distributions together. Existing connection settings and synchronized catalog tables are retained; private-updater credentials are not retained by the public distribution.
  3. Install and activate CatalogPilot Connector.
  4. Open WooCommerce > CatalogPilot in WordPress administration.
  5. Follow the setup link to connect the store to a CatalogPilot account.
  6. Create a dedicated WordPress application password for the CatalogPilot synchronization user when prompted.
  7. Complete connection verification in CatalogPilot, then use Verify Connection with CatalogPilot Account in WordPress.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require a CatalogPilot account?

Yes. The plugin is a connector for the hosted CatalogPilot service and requires a configured CatalogPilot site.

Does it require WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Where are diagnostic logs stored?

Diagnostics are disabled by default. A store manager can enable privacy-safe CatalogPilot diagnostics under WooCommerce > CatalogPilot. Messages are written through WooCommerce logging with source catalogpilot, omit credentials, customer data, catalog content, URLs, site identifiers, IP addresses, and object identifiers, and follow the store’s WooCommerce log-retention settings.

Can I install multiple CatalogPilot distributions together?

No. The private package and the public catalogpilot-connector package are alternative distributions of the same connector and must not be installed together. Deactivate and delete the installed distribution before uploading the replacement. Connection settings and synchronized catalog tables are retained. The public distribution clears private-updater credentials, so after switching back to the private distribution, run CatalogPilot Verify Install to provision private updates again.

What happens to connector data when I delete the plugin?

Deactivation and plugin deletion do not contact external services or automatically remove settings and synchronized catalog tables. This prevents data loss during updates or distribution replacement. To remove the connection permanently, disconnect the site through your CatalogPilot account, then select Permanently remove local CatalogPilot data under WooCommerce > CatalogPilot. This removes only CatalogPilot-owned data and does not alter your WooCommerce catalog.

How do I disconnect safely?

First deactivate sync, then use Disconnect in your CatalogPilot account. That server-side action fences queued work, clears the WordPress connector identity, and revokes the dedicated WordPress application password. The separate Disconnect this WordPress site action under WooCommerce > CatalogPilot clears only the local WordPress connector state and does not revoke credentials retained by your CatalogPilot account. If WordPress is unreachable, CatalogPilot records a revocation failure, blocks normal connector/updater use, and keeps the credential only so an administrator can retry. Deactivating or deleting the WordPress plugin alone never performs a remote disconnect.

What WordPress permissions does synchronization require?

Use a dedicated WordPress user with an application password. The user must have the manage_woocommerce or manage_options capability.

Does the plugin load JavaScript from a third-party server?

The plugin code and storefront runtime are packaged with the plugin and enqueued locally; no plugin JavaScript is downloaded from CatalogPilot. Approved rich descriptions can contain third-party media or allow-listed iframe embeds. An embedded page may execute its provider’s JavaScript inside that iframe, as described in the External services section.

The unminified sources corresponding to the packaged storefront runtime are included in assets/src/.

How are the packaged JavaScript files built?

The files in assets/js/ are minified from the corresponding files in assets/src/ with the GPL-compatible esbuild 0.25.9 build tool. With Node.js installed, run these commands from the plugin directory to reproduce them:

npx --yes esbuild@0.25.9 --loader=js --minify --charset=utf8 --legal-comments=none --target=es2018 < assets/src/storefront-runtime-core.js > assets/js/storefront-runtime-core.js
npx --yes esbuild@0.25.9 --loader=js --minify --charset=utf8 --legal-comments=none --target=es2018 < assets/src/woo-embed-runtime.js > assets/js/woo-embed-runtime.js
sections.changelog:
0.1.82

  • Fixed: Catalog sync exports saved product and category titles and descriptions without storefront overlays, so new source edits reach CatalogPilot while approved delivery remains enabled.
  • Fixed: Image matching strips nested WordPress size suffixes and repeated rendition markers until the URL stops changing, so images such as shoe-300×200-150×100.jpg match the same CatalogPilot image as shoe.jpg.
  • Fixed: Image matching compares image URLs in one percent-encoded form, so file names with spaces or accented characters match whether the page writes them raw or encoded. Stored image match keys are recomputed after the update in small batches, at most one per request, during admin and catalog sync requests and from a scheduled WordPress cron event, and images whose keys do not change keep matching meanwhile. After a failed batch, all recompute work waits before retrying, from one minute up to one hour, and a missing image table is recreated.
  • Fixed: Structured data keeps native WooCommerce and theme Product names unless CatalogPilot’s schema name comes from an approved title of the product, or for a variation from that variation’s own approved title; an approved name always wins. Variation names follow one order: the variation’s approved title, the variation’s own name, the parent product’s approved title, then the parent product’s name. A variation that has no name, a placeholder name such as “Default”, or just the parent product’s name moves on to the next name in that order. Only the variation’s own approved title counts as approved, so a parent product’s approved title never replaces a WooCommerce or theme variation name. Original source titles and legacy payloads no longer authorize replacing an existing name.
  • Fixed: Variation data sent to the storefront now includes the parent product’s approved title and name. When a shopper selects a variation without its own CatalogPilot data after another variation, or after opening a variation link, its structured-data name still uses the parent’s approved title. A variation named like the parent product’s stored name is not treated as having its own name.
  • Fixed: Approved CatalogPilot schema names are published as the plain text they already are, so names with literal angle brackets or entity spellings (for example “Cutlery set” or “©”) are no longer cut or decoded a second time.
  • Fixed: Structured data publishes every valid schema.org adult consideration CatalogPilot has stored, not only sexual content. Variations publish their own considerations together with their parent product’s.
  • Fixed: Fallback variation structured data names its ProductGroup after the parent product.
  • Fixed: Structured data keeps valid WooCommerce and theme SKU, GTIN and MPN values for the product being shown instead of replacing them with CatalogPilot’s; CatalogPilot only fills identifiers that are missing or invalid, keeps its own variation identifiers when the theme markup describes the parent or another variation, ignores the post ID WooCommerce uses as a SKU placeholder, and no longer adds a duplicate gtin next to a valid gtin13 (or other GTIN property).
  • Fixed: Structured data marks products as not family friendly only for sexual content. Other adult considerations remain published without creating this flag, including when older overlay data is cached.
  • Fixed: Structured data publishes a WooCommerce theme’s microdata or the merchant’s own JSON-LD isFamilyFriendly value stated as “true” or “false” (any case, or as schema.org True/False) as a real true/false value instead of text, including theme microdata written as a <link href> value. The merchant’s own flag is otherwise kept as stated, and products and product groups with sexual content are still always marked not family friendly, including the merchant’s own variation parent group, a theme adult consideration written as a <link href> value, and a schema.org address in any letter case.

0.1.81

  • Changed: Structured data treats a variation’s name as approved only when it is the variation’s own approved CatalogPilot title. A parent product’s approved title no longer counts as the variation’s approval, so a WooCommerce or theme variation name is kept over it.
  • Fixed: Variation structured-data names follow one order: the variation’s approved title, the variation’s own name, the parent product’s approved title, then the parent product’s name. A variation that has no name, a placeholder name such as “Default”, or just the parent product’s name uses the parent’s approved title before the parent’s WooCommerce name.
  • Fixed: Variation data sent to the storefront now includes the parent product’s approved title and name. When a shopper selects a variation without its own CatalogPilot data after another variation, or after opening a variation link, its structured-data name still uses the parent’s approved title. A variation named like the parent product’s stored name is not treated as having its own name.
  • Fixed: Approved CatalogPilot schema names are published as the plain text they already are, so names with literal angle brackets or entity spellings (for example “Cutlery set” or “©”) are no longer cut or decoded a second time.
  • Fixed: Structured data marks products as not family friendly only for sexual content. Other adult considerations remain published without creating this flag, including when older overlay data is cached.

0.1.79

  • Fixed: Structured data keeps native WooCommerce and theme Product names unless CatalogPilot’s schema name comes from an approved title of the product, variation or (for a variation) its parent product; an approved name always wins. Original source titles and legacy payloads no longer authorize replacing an existing name, and a variation placeholder name such as “Default” is never published. A variation whose WooCommerce name is just the parent product name is named after the parent’s approved title; as of 0.1.81 that name is not the variation’s own approval, so a matching theme variation name can still replace it.
  • Fixed: Structured data publishes every valid schema.org adult consideration CatalogPilot has stored, not only sexual content, with isFamilyFriendly false whenever one is present. Variations publish their own considerations together with their parent product’s.
  • Fixed: Fallback variation structured data names its ProductGroup after the parent product.
  • Fixed: Structured data keeps valid WooCommerce and theme SKU, GTIN and MPN values for the product being shown instead of replacing them with CatalogPilot’s; CatalogPilot only fills identifiers that are missing or invalid, keeps its own variation identifiers when the theme markup describes the parent or another variation, ignores the post ID WooCommerce uses as a SKU placeholder, and no longer adds a duplicate gtin next to a valid gtin13 (or other GTIN property).
  • Fixed: Structured data now uses approved CatalogPilot titles, descriptions and breadcrumb category names regardless of on-page display settings; display settings only control what the page shows.
  • Fixed: Approved structured-data text that is invisible or punctuation only (for example a zero-width space or an encoded non-breaking space) no longer replaces the native WooCommerce name, description or breadcrumb label.
  • Fixed: Structured-data text keeps emoji sequences, Persian and Indic joiners and right-to-left marks, keeps a literal “<” (for example “Use <5 kg bags”), and drops script and style contents.
  • Fixed: Native WooCommerce descriptions used as the structured-data fallback are kept as before, including punctuation-only, emoji-only and non-UTF-8 text.

0.1.78

  • Fixed: Preserve valid parent product descriptions shorter than 40 characters in variant schema and avoid parsing generated plain-text parent descriptions as HTML again.

0.1.77

  • Changed: Updated the CatalogPilot logo in the connector settings page.

0.1.76

  • Fixed: Shared storefront image matching ignores Lightspeed theme cache timestamps to avoid treating unchanged images as new media.

0.1.75

  • Fixed: Storefront metadata descriptions are reduced to plain text without parsing their markup in the live page, so description HTML cannot run scripts.
  • Fixed: Category schema uses the current WooCommerce category name when no enabled approved title is available, including translated categories without an approved page overlay, decoding HTML entities stored in the name. Repaired breadcrumb schema names are decoded the same way.

0.1.74

  • Merge approved category schema and CatalogPilot provenance into Rank Math named schema nodes while preserving provider node identities, graph references, and unrelated site and organization schema.

0.1.73

  • Export WooCommerce product types so catalog sync can correctly identify variable products and monitor their variants.

0.1.72

  • Restore parent product schema after clearing a variation when the initial server response identifies the page as a variant.

0.1.71

  • Restore parent product schema when a variation selected through the page URL is cleared, including select, radio, and checkbox controls.

0.1.70

  • Give selected variations their own page schema or commerce fallback instead of copying the parent product’s JSON-LD; parent GTINs are never inherited.
  • Include stored GTINs in fallback product schema and give schema images stable @id identities.
  • Attach merchant return policies to the seller Organization, including URL-only policies for All countries coverage and for a return policy URL without a chosen coverage. List every configured return policy URL as a Return Policy page, and add the policy to the connector’s seller Organization and to standalone Organization nodes passed through the connector instead of WooCommerce/Yoast/Rank Math Product schema. Keep native Offer policies and category CollectionPage containment intact.

0.1.69

  • Handle empty storefront microdata fields without interrupting structured-data processing.

0.1.68

  • Mark category JSON-LD with CatalogPilot sdPublisher provenance, including schema owned by an SEO provider, so delivery monitoring can identify CP-managed output.

0.1.67

  • Escape approved storefront titles and category labels in rendered HTML while preserving Woo Product Filter block context data.

0.1.66

  • Match WordPress scaled and thumbnail image URLs to their original image identity while retaining compatibility with existing catalog image rows.

0.1.65

  • Set the author URI to AdVision eCommerce, distinct from the CatalogPilot plugin URI.
  • Update the tested WooCommerce version to 11.1.1 after local compatibility checks.

0.1.64

  • Keep H1-only and Title-only storefront configurations from falling back to a disabled sibling heading field when the selected field has no approved value.

0.1.63

  • Fetch the local storefront payload for H1-only classic WooCommerce first loads so the enriched H1 value is available after compact bootstrap.

0.1.62

  • Honor an H1-only storefront configuration on classic WooCommerce product headings while preserving Title precedence when both fields are enabled.

0.1.61

  • Harden synchronized runtime configuration to accept data-only JSON and escape inline values.
  • Disable storefront payload diagnostics in production packages.
  • Separate WordPress.org update handling from the private updater and clear private updater state in the public build.
  • Require encrypted CatalogPilot service connections outside recognized local-development hosts.
  • Initialize each site’s catalog table schema on first run and when the connector version changes, retry failed migrations, and report unavailable storage without accepting catalog publishes.
  • Retry connector-version and updater-health settings after partial upgrade failures without rerunning completed schema work.
  • Keep partially written catalog chunks retryable when a catalog row or completed-batch marker cannot be saved.
  • Return a retryable error when connector or embed settings cannot be verified after saving.
  • Reject oversized local runtime-media requests before catalog resolution or image candidate filtering.
  • Confirm compatibility through WordPress 7.1 while retaining the WordPress 6.5 minimum.
  • Declare WooCommerce 9.2 through 11.0 compatibility in every distribution header.
  • Move CatalogPilot administration under WooCommerce and use the WooCommerce management capability.
  • Replace direct PHP error logging with optional privacy-safe WooCommerce diagnostics.
  • Lower the connector runtime floor to PHP 7.4.
  • Declare compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage; the connector does not read or write order storage or overwrite native WooCommerce catalog fields.
  • Add authenticated disconnect, application-password revocation fencing, and an explicit typed-confirmation local data purge.

0.1.60

  • Initial WordPress.org release candidate.
  • Package the storefront runtime locally and enqueue it with WordPress APIs.
  • Add separate private and WordPress.org distribution builds.
